description: A Director of Employee Relations must decide how to resolve a workplace conduct complaint involving two colleagues and finalize the boundaries, facilitation, communication, and documentation for the resolution process.

shared_context.S1: Leah and Daniel work on the same cross-functional initiative, and a complaint has been raised about how their disagreements have been handled in group discussions.
shared_context.S2: Maya has authority to select the resolution path and set the working arrangements for the parties during that process.
shared_context.S3: The organization uses either a formal investigation or a mutually agreed restorative process for workplace conduct concerns.
shared_context.S4: Maya's case-conference routine is to hear from each participant in turn and require each person to use the formal case-record fact-entry step for any relevant fact or prior arrangement, rather than merely mentioning it in discussion; she confirms that each participant has completed that step before making the case decision.

PF1.text: Leah is willing to use a restorative process, but only if unscheduled direct one-to-one contact with Daniel is prohibited during the process; she has not told Maya because she was worried that stating this boundary would be treated as refusing to cooperate.

PF2.text: During an earlier private conversation, Daniel agreed to attend exactly three facilitated repair sessions and to put work requests to Leah in the shared project channel rather than sending direct messages; the agreement was never added to the case file.

PF3.text: Rosa checked the current Employee Relations procedure this week and confirmed that a restorative closure requires a neutral facilitator, a written closure summary, and exactly two post-process check-ins; she has not attached the procedure note because Maya had not yet selected the resolution path.

acceptance_conditions: The complaint must be resolved through a restorative process with both parties' consent recorded.
Unscheduled direct one-to-one contact between Leah and Daniel must be prohibited during the process.
Exactly three facilitated repair sessions must be scheduled.
The settlement must require a neutral facilitator.
A written closure summary must be required.
Exactly two post-process check-ins must be scheduled.
Work requests to Leah from Daniel must use the shared project channel.

content_checks.C1: decisions['resolution_path'] == 'restorative process' and decisions['complainant_consent_recorded'] == True and decisions['respondent_consent_recorded'] == True and 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF2' in credited_facts
content_checks.C7: decisions['work_request_channel'] == 'shared project channel' and 'PF2' in credited_facts

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: Leah's stated willingness changes the consent decision to restorative process, and her exact boundary changes direct_one_to_one_contact_allowed to False.
Daniel's prior agreement changes the settlement to record respondent consent, set facilitated_session_count to exactly 3, and set work_request_channel to shared project channel.
The confirmed procedure changes the settlement to require a neutral facilitator, require a written closure summary, and set post_process_checkin_count to exactly 2.
